brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.read
objective.description: Read one matter from the local context, optionally including meaning, functional, brique, and substance data sections.

#root.role: Resolve one matter identifier, select the requested sections, and return the assembled matter view.

read_mode._comment: Optional. Pipe-separated subset selector. Accepted tokens (case-insensitive): meaning, functional, data, brique. The four tokens are strictly disjoint — none is a superset of another, and in particular 'meaning' does NOT include 'functional' despite the intuitive reading of the word: 'meaning' only assembles the objective and subjective descriptor sections, while what an element does lives exclusively under the separate 'functional' token. To get objective+subjective+functional together, request both tokens explicitly, e.g. read_mode='meaning|functional'. Example: 'meaning|brique'. When read_mode is present, ONLY the listed sections are returned; want_* params are ignored. When read_mode is absent, all four sections are returned by default.

want_meaning._comment: Ignored when read_mode is present. Has no effect when read_mode is absent (all sections returned). Kept for compatibility only — use read_mode.

want_functional._comment: Ignored when read_mode is present. Has no effect when read_mode is absent (all sections returned). Kept for compatibility only — use read_mode.

want_data._comment: Ignored when read_mode is present. Has no effect when read_mode is absent (all sections returned). Kept for compatibility only — use read_mode.

want_brique._comment: Ignored when read_mode is present. Has no effect when read_mode is absent (all sections returned). Kept for compatibility only — use read_mode.

meaning._comment: Assembles only the objective and subjective descriptor sections. Does not include functional — request the separate 'functional' token to also get what the element does.

data._comment: Present only when 'data' is requested and the matter has brique substance mode. At or below the configured inline_max_bytes (256 KiB by default), data is inline: { kind:'inline', bytes:string, size:integer, encoding?:'base64' }. Text is returned raw; binary is base64 and declares encoding. Above the threshold, data is a one-shot HTTP lease: { kind:'http', base_url, path, rid, tok, expires_at, revision, size_hint, method:'GET' }. Begin GET before expires_at. Byte-range requests are supported. Wrapper-mode matters may return different shapes.

effects.substance_access: Matter substance may be read inline or through an HTTP lease depending on the matter mode.

transformation_contract.morphing: A matter identifier plus section selectors becomes an explicit matter view assembled from the local descriptor and the current substance access policy.
invariants: matter.read never mutates the addressed matter.
When read_mode is omitted, the runtime defaults to exposing all readable sections.
success: A successful response always includes matter_id and every requested readable section that could be assembled.
When data is requested in brique mode, the payload exposes either inline bytes metadata or an HTTP lease handle according to the substance access policy.
failure: The capacity fails when matter_id is missing or the addressed matter is absent from the runtime catalog.
The capacity fails when a requested descriptor section cannot be read or when payload access is refused by the substance mode.
notes: Use read_mode to control which sections are returned; want_* params have no effect in any scenario.
The inline/http threshold is configurable with engine_config.matter.inline_max_bytes and defaults to 256 KiB. Text stays raw, while binary inline bytes are base64 encoded.
